# Worked example: airway, from GEO to a pipeline {#sec-worked-example}

This chapter goes from the paper to a pipeline-ready samplesheet for eight
samples of the airway dataset (four donors, untreated or dexamethasone). Budget roughly
**250 GB** of free disk while converting (it shrinks to about 20 GB of
`.fastq.gz`) and a few hours of wall time.

## 1. Find the runs

The paper (Himes *et al.* 2014) points to **GSE52778**. Its 16 samples are
four donors × four treatments (untreated, dexamethasone, albuterol, both). We
want untreated and Dex only. From Run Selector
(`https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Traces/study/?acc=GSE52778`), or ENA:

| Run | GSM | sample_title | Donor | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SRR1039508 | GSM1275862 | N61311_untreated | N61311 | untrt |
| SRR1039509 | GSM1275863 | N61311_Dex | N61311 | dex |
| SRR1039512 | GSM1275866 | N052611_untreated | N052611 | untrt |
| SRR1039513 | GSM1275867 | N052611_Dex | N052611 | dex |
| SRR1039516 | GSM1275870 | N080611_untreated | N080611 | untrt |
| SRR1039517 | GSM1275871 | N080611_Dex | N080611 | dex |
| SRR1039520 | GSM1275874 | N061011_untreated | N061011 | untrt |
| SRR1039521 | GSM1275875 | N061011_Dex | N061011 | dex |

Each GSM has exactly one run, all `PAIRED`, 2 × 63 bp. The two files in this
repository's `examples/` folder hold exactly this:

- `examples/airway_SRR_Acc_List.txt`: the eight runs
- `examples/airway_runs_to_samples.tsv`: run → sample name

## 2. Download

Set up a folder (anywhere with ~250 GB free):

```bash
cd /path/with/space        # laptop folder, external drive, or cluster scratch
git clone https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data.git
mkdir -p airway/logs && cd airway
cp ../download-public-data/examples/airway_* .
```

Then pick **one** way to download:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## From ENA (any computer, no toolkit)

```bash
while read -r acc; do
  bash ../download-public-data/scripts/ena_download.sh "$acc" fastq
done < airway_SRR_Acc_List.txt
```

ENA files are already gzipped and MD5-checked. Then make the read-count table
the next steps use:

```bash
for f in fastq/*.fastq.gz; do echo -e "$(basename $f)\t$(( $(zcat < $f | wc -l) / 4 ))"; done > fastq/read_counts.tsv
```

## SRA Toolkit, simple loop (any computer)

Use Route A from [Downloading many runs](at-scale.qmd#route-a-a-simple-loop-any-computer),
with `SRR_Acc_List.txt` replaced by `airway_SRR_Acc_List.txt`.

## SRA Toolkit, SLURM cluster

```bash
sbatch --array=1-8%4 ../download-public-data/scripts/download_sra.sh airway_SRR_Acc_List.txt fastq
```
:::

When the downloads finish:

```bash
ls fastq/
cat fastq/read_counts.tsv | sort
```

A few airway runs also produce an orphan-read file (`SRR....fastq.gz`) next
to `_1` and `_2`. That's expected ([split-3](fasterq-dump.qmd#what-files-you-get-split-3)).
Check it's small compared with `_1`.

## 3. Merge and rename

Here there's one run per sample, so this is just a rename, but the same
command handles multi-run samples:

```bash
bash ../download-public-data/scripts/merge_runs.sh airway_runs_to_samples.tsv fastq merged
ls merged/
# N052611_dex_R1_001.fastq.gz  N052611_dex_R2_001.fastq.gz  N052611_untrt_R1_001.fastq.gz ...
```

## 4. Write a samplesheet

Every pipeline wants a table that says which files belong to which sample and
condition. The columns differ between pipelines; here is one for
[bagPipes](https://github.com/PhanstielLab/bagPipes) `RNApipe` (a Snakemake
pipeline for SLURM clusters), built from the run table. bagPipes needs `Read1`, `Read2` and `Sequencing_Directory`, plus whatever
metadata columns your `fileNamesFrom` and `mergeBy` use. Build it from the
run table:

```bash
DIR=$PWD/merged/
{
  printf "Project\tCell_Type\tDonor\tTreatment\tBio_Rep\tRead1\tRead2\tSequencing_Directory\n"
  tail -n +2 airway_runs_to_samples.tsv | while IFS=$'\t' read -r run sample; do
    donor=${sample%_*}; trt=${sample#*_}
    printf "airway\tASM\t%s\t%s\t1\t%s_R1_001.fastq.gz\t%s_R2_001.fastq.gz\t%s\n" \
      "$donor" "$trt" "$sample" "$sample" "$DIR"
  done
} > RNAsamplesheet.txt
column -t RNAsamplesheet.txt
```

And in `config/RNAconfig.yaml`:

```yaml
samplesheet: '/path/with/space/airway/RNAsamplesheet.txt'
fileNamesFrom: ['Project', 'Cell_Type', 'Donor', 'Treatment']
mergeBy: ['Project', 'Cell_Type', 'Treatment']    # one merged track per treatment
```

Choose the hg38 reference block, and check the library type after the first run
(Salmon's `lib_format_counts.json`). If it is `IU`, the library is unstranded:
set `stranded: False`. Then `sbatch RNApipe.sh`, as in
[omics-walkthru: Running RNApipe](https://jpflores-13.github.io/omics-walkthru/rna-seq/running-rnapipe.html).

For other pipelines, the same information goes into their own format. For
example, [nf-core/rnaseq](https://nf-co.re/rnaseq) wants a CSV with
`sample,fastq_1,fastq_2,strandedness`:

```bash
{
  echo "sample,fastq_1,fastq_2,strandedness"
  tail -n +2 airway_runs_to_samples.tsv | while IFS=$'\t' read -r run sample; do
    echo "$sample,$DIR${sample}_R1_001.fastq.gz,$DIR${sample}_R2_001.fastq.gz,auto"
  done
} > nfcore_samplesheet.csv
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## In DESeq2

Donors differ a lot from each other, so include donor in the design to compare
treatments *within* donors: `design = ~ Donor + Treatment`.
:::

## 5. Keep the record

```bash
fasterq-dump --version > sra_tools_version.txt
mkdir -p /path/to/permanent/storage/GSE52778
rsync -av merged/ airway_* fastq/read_counts.tsv sra_tools_version.txt /path/to/permanent/storage/GSE52778/
```
